claims.text: For \((r,q,i,j)=(5,3,2,2)\), \(a=1,b=2,N=\binom31=3\), and the two families are \(F_1=(22,32,33)\) and \(F_2=(22,221,222)\). [artifact e03b87dfaac58fc8c68b65e28c061cd1ac2d9a04b2e72c5e80e07ffd2ad7d00f]

In the \(3^5\)-box, the Schur-span module for shapes containing \(22\) has \(40\) ordered Schur columns. For \(F_1\), the complementary-column order is \[ \begin{gathered} 221;2211,222,321;22111,2221,3211,322,331;\\ 22211,2222,32111,3221,3311,332; 22221,32211,3222,33111,3321,333;\\ 22222,32221,33211,3322,3331; 32222,33221,33311,3332; 33222,33321,3333;33322,33331;33332;33333 . \end{gathered} \] The selected Pieri rows in the retained artifact order give a \(37\times37\) complementary minor of absolute determinant \(1\). [artifact e03b87dfaac58fc8c68b65e28c061cd1ac2d9a04b2e72c5e80e07ffd2ad7d00f]

The separately formed direct-LR relation rows reduce integrally to the selected Pieri rows: the artifact retains, for each LR row, its integer coefficient vector in the fixed selected-row order. Hence the LR and selected-Pieri relation lattices agree for both \(F_1\) and \(F_2\). [artifact e03b87dfaac58fc8c68b65e28c061cd1ac2d9a04b2e72c5e80e07ffd2ad7d00f]

The resulting Smith quotients are torsion-free of rank \(3\): \[ J_{v_{5,5,4,8}}/\Lambda_+J_{v_{5,5,4,8}}\cong\mathbb Z^3, \] with respective bases given by the images of \(F_1\) and \(F_2\), subject to the standard integral box-model identification of this quotient. [artifact e03b87dfaac58fc8c68b65e28c061cd1ac2d9a04b2e72c5e80e07ffd2ad7d00f]
